figures.alt: Downspout connected to a buried drain pipe and cleanout beside a Florida home
figures.caption: Flat, sandy lots need a planned discharge route. Start at the downspout and determine where water can go without returning to the foundation.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Gutter corner and downspout transition at a Florida stucco home
figures.caption: Keep the buried pipe at a steady grade away from the house. A dip in the route traps water and silt instead of carrying runoff outward.

figures.alt: Downspout discharge transitioning to a shallow swale away from a foundation
figures.caption: Drainage work is judged by where water ends up, not only by the pipe installation. Confirm the discharge point and local requirements before opening a route.
